In early March, 2020, my business partner would send texts daily about how travel was getting crushed. Every day I would check our numbers and still see growth of 100% YOY with minor drops and dips and then growth again.  We were trending with our projected growth. Then, March 15 (the ides of March) hit and our sales plummeted, down -55%. By March 21 sales were down -87.5%.  We were getting crushed. I can share these specific numbers because Stripe has a great UI and it is super simple to grab this data. Stripe makes looking at numbers simple, and it makes setting up a PCI compliant payment processor super easy for dev teams.  Stripe makes themselves sticky. So sticky that they can try to pull what comes next.

item.title: Did Google's Workspace Redesign Make Its Icons Easier for AI to See?
item.content:encoded: Google's 2026 Workspace icon redesign didn't just improve human usability—it also improved machine perception. By comparing old and new icons across OpenCLIP, SigLIP, and DINOv2, I found that the redesigned icons are consistently more separated in embedding space. The biggest gains came from Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Forms, which were previously clustered together due to nearly identical shapes and colors. As software agents increasingly rely on vision rather than DOM access, embedding separability may become an important design consideration for UI assets.

New products – especially those driven by community – are incredibly fragile.

7 days ago we launched a beta of YourStack (with a grammatically incorrect, non-editable tweet – lol). Instantly those same nostalgic feelings from the early days of Product Hunt re-emerged. The response has been very encouraging. Alex was kind enough to write about it on BuzzFeed. Lucas followed with a story on TechCrunch. And a bunch of folks shared support on Twitter and Product Hunt.

But the product is very early and our roadmap is deep. So far we've onboarded only ~4% of those that have signed up as we build tooling to scale (thanks for all your patience!). I wake up each morning nervous but excited to read your feedback and wild ideas as the team and I continue building.

If you get a chance, create your account and start stacking. We're whitelisting new friendly folks each day.

item.title: Universal Basic Income Was Always Controversial - AI Just Changed The Entire Argument
item.content:encoded:
AI is changing the Universal Basic Income debate from a philosophical discussion into a practical economic question.
Historically, technology displaced some jobs but created others. The concern with AI is that it may reduce demand for human labor faster than new opportunities emerge.
Supporters argue UBI could provide economic stability, maintain consumer spending, and help society adapt during a period of unprecedented automation. Critics worry about funding, incentives, capital flight, inflation, and the long-term social consequences of decoupling income from work.
The biggest challenge may not be whether UBI works, but whether governments can implement solutions before disruption arrives. If AI significantly alters the relationship between labor and economic value, societies may be forced to rethink how wealth is distributed, how work is valued, and what role humans play in an increasingly automated economy.
The question is no longer whether AI can do the work. The question is what happens to an economy built around human earnings if it can.

item.title: Out of 2,159 Cold Messages, Only 4 People Replied
item.content:encoded: I spent five weeks trying to validate startup ideas the hard way. The numbers: 2,159 LinkedIn connection requests, 766 accepts, ~575 personalized follow-ups, and 4 genuine replies (a 0.7% reply rate, one real conversation per 540 requests). Zero confirmed "I'd pay for this." Of 3 ideas, I've killed 1 and 2 are still alive. I logged 27 validation signals, but 8 were red flags, almost as many reasons to stop as to keep going. Total spend: about $261. The kicker: to manage the hunt I built my own CRM from scratch, ~5,800 lines in two days. I built a product to help me look for a product. This is what starting on your own actually looks like, minus the montage.
